newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close sharply higher on financials.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close sharply higher on financials.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished sharply higher on Wednesday on strong buying in the heavily weighted financial sector that brokers said appeared to have been orchestrated by government-related funds.
The weighted index surged as high as 8,191.59 -- a rise of more than three percent -- in late trading but the momentum eased minutes before the close.
At the close, the index was 229.50 points or 2.89 percent higher at 8,181.62 points, having regained about three-fourths of what it lost in a shock 3.72 percent downturn on Monday.
Turnover was a relatively muted T$112.43 billion.
Financials, which had lagged previous gains and were hit hard in Monday's big selloff, were extremely strong. The sector far outperformed the market, jumping 4.93 percent.

Liu Tai-ying, chairman of the ruling Nationalist Party's business management committee and affiliated China Development Corp, would not comment on rumours of big intervention by billion-dollar investment firms under his control.
"I cannot tell you. It's a secret," Liu told reporters.
Liu's China Development rose by as much as T$5 during the session but closed at T$118.5, a gain of $1.5 or 1.28 percent.
Analysts said the government's handiwork seemed obvious.
"There is apparently intervention by the government," said Chen Han-chung, an analyst at Yungli Securities.
Brokers said some investors snapped up bargains.

They cautioned that confidence had not fully recovered as jitters over public safety and political uncertainty were likely to intensify after revelations that another teenager had been kidnapped and murdered -- the second such killing in a month.
Worries over a spate of serious crimes, some still unsolved after months of investigation, have precipitated a government crisis that resulted on Wednesday in a minor cabinet shakeup.
